$comment: Controlled vocabulary mapping a termination condition (the measured quantity + the direction the limit is approached from) to the EMMO termination quantity class, attached under hasTerminationParameter. This replaces the old name-encoded scheme (e.g. 'discharging_cutoff_voltage' -> LowerVoltageLimit) with an explicit (quantity, direction) pair, mirroring bmgen's LOWER_LIMITS/UPPER_LIMITS remap. 'below'/'above' = the value is a lower/upper bound the channel crosses to end the step; a cutoff with no direction takes the 'below' entry. 'duration' is time-based and direction-free. 'current_density' is not a quantity an author writes: a 'current' cutoff stated per area (mA/cm2, A/m2) is a current density, and the emitters type it with these classes. A 'current' cutoff in a unit of another quantity (V, C, Ah) takes the 'generic' class: a current limit class would claim an electric current. C-rate and capacity cutoffs have no limit class of their own. Every emmo_class resolves in the v1 records context and in the bundled EMMO context (tests/test_mapping_governance.py).
